sentences.text: Fossils of Heteropetalus are exceptionally well preserved, revealing soft tissue details like eyes and a gill cover. This small fish reached a maximum length of 12 centimeters and possessed a scaleless, torpedo-shaped body with a diphycercal tail fin — a fin type where the upper and lower lobes merge at the base.
Evidence of blood vessels in fossilized gills indicates these fish died by asphyxiation after being buried by mud.
The species Heteropetalus elegantulus was named in 1977 by Richard Lund from fossils found in the Bear Gulch Limestone of Montana.

Males had larger, modified dorsal fins with hook-like organs, indicating sexual dimorphism. Researchers suggest the hook-like structure on male dorsal fins functioned as a clasper to grab females during mating.
Recent research places Heteropetalus in the order Debeeriiformes and family Debeeriidae based on similarities to Debeerius.
Heteropetalus lived during the Serpukhovian stage, between 326.9 and 323.6 million years ago.
